records.title: 12V Auxiliary Battery Drain from Module Wake Cycles
records.description: The Lyriq's numerous electronic modules perform periodic wake cycles that can drain the 12V auxiliary battery when the vehicle sits for extended periods. Owners report dead 12V batteries after 5-10 days of sitting, preventing the vehicle from being unlocked or started.
records.solution: A dealer software update addresses excessive module wake frequency. For long-term storage, connect a 12V battery maintainer to the auxiliary battery access point. GM released a TSB addressing this issue.
symptoms: Dead battery after sitting several days
Key fob won't unlock doors
Vehicle won't power on
Infotainment slow to boot after sitting
12V battery warning on app
Multiple warning messages on startup after jump

communityRecommendations.content: Ask the dealer for the latest software update addressing parasitic 12V drain — multiple revisions have been released

records.title: ABS Releases Brake Pressure / Reduced Braking at Low Speeds (Recall 24V589)
records.description: On 2023-2024 Lyriq AWD (dual-motor) models, a software defect in the Electronic Brake Control Module can falsely detect wheel slip during braking on dry surfaces below 25 mph. When ABS falsely activates, it can keep releasing hydraulic brake pressure, causing reduced stopping performance or near-loss of service braking. GM recalled about 21,469 AWD units in the U.S.; single-motor RWD models are not affected.
records.solution: GM's remedy is a free software update to the Electronic Brake Control Module (EBCM), delivered over-the-air or at a dealer under recall 24V589 (GM N242453471). Affected vehicles were built December 2022 through August 2024; confirm by VIN at NHTSA.
symptoms: Brake pedal feels like it loses pressure during low-speed stops
Increased stopping distance on dry pavement under 25 mph
ABS activating when it shouldn't during gentle braking
Momentary loss of braking feel

records.title: Charge Port Door and Charging Session Issues
records.description: Some Lyriq owners report intermittent charging issues including the charge port door not opening or closing properly, charging sessions stopping unexpectedly, and difficulty with certain DC fast chargers. The motorized charge port door can stick or fail to actuate in cold weather. Some Level 2 and DC fast charging stations have compatibility issues with the Lyriq's charging module. GM has addressed many of these with software updates.
records.solution: Install latest OTA software updates which address many charging compatibility issues. For stuck charge port doors, the manual release inside the cargo area allows manual opening. GM dealers can recalibrate the charge port motor. For DC fast charging issues, try different charging networks - the Lyriq works best with EVgo and ChargePoint stations. Cold weather can cause the door to stick - a silicone spray on the door seal helps.
symptoms: Charge port door won't open when pressed
Charging session stops unexpectedly before completion
Error message when attempting to charge at certain stations
Charge port door stuck open or closed
Slow charging speed on DC fast charger

citations.title: NHTSA Complaint #11539844 - 2024 Cadillac Lyriq charging system / charge port concerns

communityRecommendations.content: GM Service Campaign N232409680 covers free charge port housing replacement (part 86812523, revised design) for affected Lyriqs. Contact dealer with VIN to check eligibility. The revised design addresses the latch mechanism that fails to release the charging plug

Prevent cold-weather charge port freezing by applying dielectric grease on door seal before winter. Manual emergency release cord located in cargo floor under left panel - familiarize yourself with its location before you need it. Some owners pre-heat cabin before unplugging in freezing temperatures

If charging session stops unexpectedly, check for pending OTA updates first - several charging software updates have been released. Try a different charging network to rule out station compatibility. Pre-condition battery in cold weather before attempting DCFC - cold battery will either refuse fast charge or charge very slowly

records.title: Front Stabilizer Bar Bracket Bolts Loosen and Separate (Recall 25V232)
records.description: On certain 2023-2025 Lyriqs, the left and/or right front stabilizer (sway) bar bracket bolts were improperly torqued at the factory because of a fastening-tool software logic error, allowing them to loosen and separate from the frame. A detached stabilizer bar or bracket can damage high-voltage cables or EV battery coolant lines, potentially causing the vehicle to shut off and lose drive power over time.
records.solution: Dealers inspect and, as needed, properly re-fasten (or replace) the front stabilizer bar bracket bolts free of charge under recall 25V232 (GM N252494190). The factory fastening-tool logic was corrected in January 2025; owner letters were mailed May 26, 2025.
symptoms: Clunking or rattling from the front suspension over bumps
Loose or vague handling / increased body roll in corners
Visible loose or missing stabilizer bar bracket bolts
Possible loss of drive power if coolant lines or HV cables are damaged

records.title: Heat Pump / Climate System Failure and No Heat in Extreme Cold
records.description: Owners report recurring Lyriq climate-control failures, including loss of cabin heat in extreme cold, with some vehicles failing repeatedly for the same fault. Documented causes include an incorrect HVAC coolant sensor harness on certain 2024 RWD units (wires stressed at the connector) and temperature-control communication faults, with readings reported to swing after DC fast charging.
records.solution: For the coolant sensor harness defect (GM service update N232414770, about 557 affected 2024 RWD units), dealers perform a harness clip adjustment/replacement. Communication-fault and fast-charge sensor-conflict issues are addressed via control-module software updates. Have the dealer diagnose the specific fault and apply the latest HVAC/thermal-management software.
symptoms: No or weak cabin heat in cold weather despite running the heater
Climate system repeatedly fails with the same fault
Temperature control / communication fault codes (e.g. reported E-378)
Erratic cabin temperature readings after DC fast charging
High range loss in winter (heat pump and thermal load draining the battery)

records.title: Inconsistent DC Fast-Charging Speed With Mid-Session Power Dips
records.description: Independent testing (including Tom Moloughney / InsideEVs) and owner-logged curves show the Lyriq peaks near 188-190 kW on a healthy 150-350 kW DC fast charger but suffers abrupt power plunges mid-session (notably around 52% and again near 77-80% state of charge), dragging the 10-80% average down to roughly 90-130 kW. The 400-volt architecture means a 350 kW charger gives no advantage over a 150 kW unit, so fast-charge stops take longer than the headline rate suggests.
records.solution: Precondition the battery before a DC fast-charge stop to reach and hold higher rates. Much of the behavior is inherent to the Lyriq's charge curve, but keep the vehicle software current (GM has tuned thermal/charging logic via OTA updates), choose an uncongested high-power charger, and report persistently abnormal low rates to a dealer to rule out a thermal-management fault.
symptoms: Charging speed drops sharply mid-session (around 50% and 77-80% SoC)
Lower-than-expected 10-80% average charge rate
350 kW charger no faster than a 150 kW charger
Longer-than-advertised fast-charge stop times (about 40 min 20-80%)

records.title: Instrument Cluster Display Goes Blank While Driving (Recall 25V356)
records.description: A software error in the video display control module can cause the 33-inch driver instrument cluster to intermittently go blank while driving, removing the speedometer, warning lights, and rearview camera image. GM recalled about 41,376 Lyriqs (3,318 from 2023 and 38,058 from 2024, built March 2022 through September 2024). NHTSA estimates roughly 3% of recalled vehicles actually have the defect.
records.solution: GM's remedy is a free software update to the video display control module, delivered over-the-air (OTA) or installed at a Cadillac dealer under recall 25V356 (GM N252500680). Owner notification letters were mailed July 14, 2025. Verify your VIN at recalls.nhtsa.dot.gov.
symptoms: Driver instrument cluster goes black or blank while driving
Speedometer and gauges disappear intermittently
Cluster reboots or flickers, sometimes returning on its own
Loss of warning lights, trip information, and rearview camera image

records.title: Inaccurate Range Estimation in Cold Weather
records.description: The Lyriq range estimator significantly overestimates available range in cold weather, leading to range anxiety and potential strandings. The algorithm does not adequately account for cabin heating load, battery thermal management, and reduced battery chemistry efficiency in temperatures below 40F.
records.solution: GM has released OTA updates improving cold-weather range estimation accuracy. Pre-condition the battery while plugged in before departing in cold weather. Plan routes with 30% additional buffer in winter. Use the heated seats and steering wheel instead of cabin heat to maximize range.
symptoms: Range drops faster than predicted
Displayed range much higher than actual
Significant range loss in cold weather
Range estimate fluctuates widely

records.title: Rear Camera and Surround Vision System Intermittent Failure
records.description: The rear camera and surround vision system intermittently displays a black or distorted image when engaging Reverse. The camera feeds may freeze, show the wrong camera angle, or display a "Rear Camera Unavailable" message. The issue is software-related and typically resolves after a vehicle restart.
records.solution: Apply the latest OTA software updates. If the issue persists, the dealer can reflash the camera control module. Check for moisture in the rear camera housing — condensation can affect image quality. A hard reset of the vehicle (park, lock, wait 5 minutes) usually restores camera function temporarily.
symptoms: Black screen when in Reverse
Distorted camera image
Rear camera unavailable message
Surround vision showing wrong angle
Camera image freezes

records.title: Rear Seat Belt Anchor Bracket Improperly Welded (Recall 23V785)
records.description: On 2023-2024 Lyriqs built March 14 through July 22, 2023, the bracket that anchors the left-rear and center-rear seat belts may have been improperly welded to the seat frame because the supplier misaligned the bracket, producing weaker welds that could fail under crash loads. An improperly welded bracket may not restrain a rear occupant as intended, increasing injury risk. About 43 units are affected.
records.solution: Dealers replace the rear seat cushion frame free of charge under recall 23V785. Until repaired, owners are advised not to use the left-rear and center-rear seating positions (the right-rear belt is correctly welded). Owner letters were mailed January 17, 2024.
symptoms: Affected rear seat belt anchorage may not hold in a crash
Recall advisory to avoid left-rear and center-rear seats until repaired
No driver-noticeable symptom — VIN-based recall identification
